entries.context: A reusable practical capability for improving a decision process, not a shortcut or trick.
entries.grammarNotes: Use sentence case in body copy. Keep the English alias only where recognition or cross-language mapping helps.
entries.example: Cette compétence de décision aide à comparer plusieurs options avant de choisir.

entries.context: A label that describes how strong or complete the supporting evidence is. It must not imply certainty when the canonical evidence is limited.
entries.grammarNotes: Prefer the same wording across cards, detail pages and machine-readable labels when natural grammar allows it.
entries.example: Le niveau de preuve est limité : cette technique doit être utilisée avec prudence.

entries.context: Language and semantic review has been completed according to the project contract. It is not a legal certification and does not upgrade evidence quality.
entries.grammarNotes: Use the shorter form in status labels; explain the scope in documentation when needed.
entries.example: Cette version française est une localisation relue du contenu canonique anglais.

entries.context: The localized record no longer matches the required canonical source revision. This state does not automatically mean the old translation is factually wrong.
entries.grammarNotes: Prefer a user-facing action phrase over a technical database adjective when displayed in UI.
entries.example: Cette localisation est à mettre à jour après une modification du contenu source.

note: This file illustrates the data shape. Real projects should build their glossary from their own domain corpus, audience and target-language usage rather than copying these terms.
